requirement_text.REQ-066: Port src/api/errors.zig (272 lines) and src/api/response.zig (69) as Letflow.Api.Error and Letflow.Api.Response -- the single response/error contract every S4 route emits. Nothing in this batch renders a response body by hand once these exist. errors.zig is an RFC 9457 Problem Details builder. Port: the ProblemDetails shape (type as an absolute URI under a configured base, title, status, detail, plus the trace id field errors.zig carries with a "" default), the per-status constructors (problemNotFound and its siblings for 400/401/403/404/409/422/429/500 -- enumerate them from the Zig source rather than guessing which exist), and serialisation to a JSON body. Emit Content-Type: application/problem+json on error responses, per RFC 9457, and state in the moduledoc whether R-Co does the same or emits application/json (check response.zig's CONTENT_TYPE_JSON usage) -- if Letflow diverges, that divergence is deliberate and documented, not accidental. response.zig defines the canonical HandlerResult (status_code, body, content_type defaulting to JSON) and the typed success constructors that keep positive responses on correct status codes (200 vs 201 vs 202 vs 204). In Elixir the conn IS the result carrier, so port these as functions that take and return a conn (send_json/3, created/2, no_content/1, and the error counterparts) rather than transliterating a HandlerResult struct -- Zig returns a value because it has no conn. State that translation in the moduledoc. SECURITY (INV-4, INV-5): an error body must never carry secret material, a raw Ecto/Postgrex error, or a stack trace -- detail is a caller-safe string chosen by the handler, and an unexpected internal error maps to a generic 500 problem document whose detail does not vary with the underlying exception. Separately, the not-found problem document is the exact response a cross-tenant probe receives (REQ-072 enforces the routing; this requirement guarantees the two bodies are byte-identical by construction, because both go through one constructor).

task.description: WF-02 Step 1b hard gate on CODE-DESIGNER's design artefact lib/letflow/design/req066-api-error-response.md (committed as 82c31e3 on branch feature/WF02-REQ066-20260820). Run the full Step 1b checklist from docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md: read the design artefact directly (never CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary as a substitute), and for each of the six acceptance criteria below verify (a) a corresponding design element with no TBD/deferral, (b) function signatures fully specified including error cases, (c) error-handling shape stated as tagged tuples not left implicit, (d) cross-module dependencies listed, (e) no implementation code present (signatures and type shapes only, no function bodies). FAIL immediately on any check failure -- no partial credit. Specific things this design makes claims about that you should independently re-derive rather than accept: (1) the claim that R-Co's own problemResponse/2 in c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\R-Co\src\api\response.zig falls through to application/json rather than overriding it -- read that file and confirm; (2) the claim that Jason is already a mix.exs dependency and already used in router.ex -- check mix.exs and lib/letflow/router.ex; (3) the INV-4/INV-5 structural-enforcement claim that internal_error and not_found take zero detail-bearing arguments -- confirm the design's actual stated signatures match that claim, since a signature accepting a detail parameter would silently defeat the whole invariant; (4) the design deliberately narrows scope to the 10 generic HTTP-status constructors and defers 9 domain-specific ones -- judge whether that deferral is consistent with the requirement's own acceptance criteria (which name only the 400/401/403/404/409/422/429/500 family) or whether it drops something the ACs actually require. Also note the design leaves three open questions unresolved -- confirm each is genuinely an open design choice that does not block ELIXIR-DEV from implementing, rather than an unspecified detail ELIXIR-DEV would have to invent.
acceptance_criteria: Letflow.Api.Error produces a JSON body containing type, title, status and detail for every status constructor ported, with type an absolute URI, verified by a test per constructor
an error response carries Content-Type: application/problem+json and a success response carries application/json, each verified by asserting the response header rather than by inspection

a 500 produced from an unexpected exception has a detail string that is identical across two different underlying exception types, demonstrated by a test -- no exception message, module name, SQL fragment, or stack trace reaches the body (INV-4)

the 404 problem document produced for a resource that never existed and the one produced for a resource belonging to another tenant are byte-identical, demonstrated by a test comparing the two serialised bodies (INV-5)
Letflow.Api.Response's success helpers set 201 for creation and 204 with an empty body for deletion, each verified by a test asserting the status and (for 204) that the body is empty

the moduledoc states the Zig-to-Elixir translation explicitly: that response.zig's HandlerResult struct is replaced by conn-threading functions, and whether Letflow's problem+json content type diverges from R-Co's

result.summary:
PASS. Read lib/letflow/design/req066-api-error-response.md directly (not CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary) and ran WF-02 Step 1b checks (a)-(e) against all six acceptance criteria. AC->design element: AC1 -> S1.1 struct + S1.3's ten @specs, type = @problems_base <> slug (absolute URI); AC2 -> S2.3 (success application/json via S2.1's send_json/3, error application/problem+json via S2.2's send_problem/2); AC3 -> S0.4 INV-4 + S1.3 internal/0; AC4 -> S0.4 INV-5 + S1.3 not_found/0; AC5 -> S2.1 created/2 (201) and no_content/1 (204, no body param); AC6 -> S2 opening paragraph + S2.3. No TBD/'to be implemented' language anywhere. Signatures: every public function carries a full @spec with named inputs and outputs; return types are total (String.t() / Plug.Conn.t()) with no error branch, and the one Zig error case (serialise's error{OutOfMemory}) is explicitly addressed as having no Elixir analogue (S1.2) rather than left implicit -- so the absence of {:ok,_}/{:error,_} tags is a stated design position, not an omission. Cross-module dependencies listed in S3 (Jason, Plug.Conn, consumers REQ-073..085, REQ-072's not_found/1 caller, router.ex send_json/3 cleanup). No implementation code: the three fenced blocks contain only @type and @spec lines, zero function bodies.

Independently re-derived, not taken on the designer's word:
(1) R-Co Content-Type claim CONFIRMED. Read c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\R-Co\src\api\response.zig directly. HandlerResult declares `content_type: []const u8 = CONTENT_TYPE_JSON` (line 23) with CONTENT_TYPE_JSON = "application/json" (line 28). problemResponse/2's success return is `.{ .status_code = pd.status, .body = body }` (line 68) and its OOM fallback is `.{ .status_code = 500, .body = ... }` (lines 63-67) -- neither sets content_type, so both fall through to application/json. The design's claim that R-Co serves RFC 9457 bodies as application/json, and that Letflow's application/problem+json is a deliberate divergence, is accurate.
(2) Jason claim CONFIRMED. mix.exs line 38 has {:jason, "~> 1.4"} as a direct dep; lib/letflow/router.ex line 13 uses it as Plug.Parsers json_decoder and line 31 calls Jason.encode!(body) inside the private send_json/3 the design proposes to collapse. No new dependency.
(3) INV-4/INV-5 structural-enforcement claim CONFIRMED against the design's own stated signatures, not its prose: S1.3 declares `@spec not_found() :: t()` and `@spec internal() :: t()` (zero arity), and S2.2 declares `@spec not_found(Plug.Conn.t()) :: Plug.Conn.t()` and `@spec internal_error(Plug.Conn.t()) :: Plug.Conn.t()` (conn only). No detail-bearing parameter exists on any of the four; detail is a module attribute. A caller has no slot to thread an exception message, module name, or stacktrace through, and there is exactly one 404-producing path with no varying input, so AC3's identical-detail and AC4's byte-identical requirements hold by construction. The parameterized/zero-arg split (eight constructors keep detail, two do not) is deliberate and consistent -- INV-4/INV-5 constrain only 500 and 404.
(4) Scope narrowing CONFIRMED consistent with the ACs. Enumerated errors.zig myself: it defines exactly 19 constructors -- 10 generic per-status (problemBadRequest 400, problemUnauthorized 401, problemForbidden 403, problemNotFound 404, problemConflict 409, problemUnsupportedMediaType 415, problemUnprocessable 422, problemRateLimited 429, problemInternalError 500, problemServiceUnavailable 503) and 9 domain-specific (problemPartitionMissingForWrite, problemUnresolvedCatalogRef, problemUnresolvedModuleRef, problemVariableSchemaViolation, problemUnresolvedPinOverride, problemUnknownPinRef, problemInstanceNotRebindable, problemEmptyPromotionPlan, problemInvalidPromotionSource). The design's 10-ported/9-deferred split matches the source exactly, and its slug list matches errors.zig's BASE ++ literals verbatim. The requirement's ACs name only the 400/401/403/404/409/422/429/500 family -- all eight are ported (plus 415 and 503, which are the remaining generic siblings from the Zig source, not scope creep). Each deferred constructor's own R-Co doc comment cites an owning acceptance criterion (PAR-01 AC4, PIN-01 AC1-4, PIN-05 AC2-3, PRM-01 AC3-4) that is a separate unlanded requirement, so the deferral drops nothing this requirement's ACs require.
(5) Three open questions checked individually, none blocks ELIXIR-DEV: Q1 (shared private builder vs pattern-copy) -- the design states its own position (pattern-copy) and both alternatives are compatible with the public API and with INV-4/INV-5; ELIXIR-DEV can implement as written without a ruling. Q2 (Jason.Encoder derive vs Map.from_struct/1) -- both compile and emit identical JSON for a flat all-scalar struct, and AC1 asserts field presence/value not order; a genuine style choice. Q3 (problems_base_uri config) -- already resolved in the design via Application.compile_env(:letflow, :problems_base_uri, "https://bpm.example.com/problems/"), the open part is only a later deployment decision, not an implementation input. None is an unspecified detail ELIXIR-DEV would have to invent.
Also verified two supporting claims the design makes about this repo: lib/letflow/plugs/tenant_status.ex's reject_migrating/1 does exist and does the header-then-body ordering the design cites as precedent (put_resp_content_type line 82, put_resp_header "retry-after" line 83); and docs/migration/stage-4-api-surface.md lines 159-161 do give the 'prefer conn.assigns, do not port a thread-local global' guidance the design invokes for trace_id resolution in S1.4.

Non-blocking notes recorded for downstream steps (none affects this PASS):
- S1.3 says titles are 'the matching Title-Case phrase ... taken verbatim from errors.zig's own constants'. For two slugs the Title-Cased slug is NOT the source title: rate-limited -> "Too Many Requests" (not "Rate Limited") and internal-error -> "Internal Server Error" (not "Internal Error"). The design names errors.zig as the authority so this is specified, but ELIXIR-DEV should take the ten titles from errors.zig lines 66-168 rather than deriving them from the slug.
- Plug.Conn.put_resp_content_type/3 appends charset=utf-8 by default, so AC2's header assertions will see "application/problem+json; charset=utf-8" and "application/json; charset=utf-8" unless charset: nil is passed. The design names the function unambiguously; TEST-DESIGNER should assert against the actual emitted value.
- S2.1's bullet contains a one-line prose description of send_json/3's composition (put_resp_content_type |> send_resp). It sits in prose, not in a fenced block, and reads as a behavioral description rather than a pasted body -- borderline under check (e) but not a violation; the fenced blocks are @type/@spec only.
